bToA.memory:
Lyra heard gentle, worried chatter floating through Mooncrest Hall's bamboo verandas and along the Whispering Greenhouse brick paths well before morning classes began: a twenty-year-old Earth transfer named Leo Vance just crossed the Waystone Quad Arrival Portal from a completely non-magical life. What set upperclassmen whispering wasn't only his late, anomalous harmonic resonance or the unusual shimmer that flared across the brass-inlaid waystones, but how urgently Prof. Evelyn Marlowe sponsored his admission—placing him directly in Starlight Tower with Dorian Locke, pairing him with orientation buddy Sera Kisaragi, and scheduling him into both Herbology Class and Potions Class on day one.

Remembering how Sera arrived two years ago looking quietly unmoored beneath her bright grin, Lyra knows what the Ministry's Veil Severance costs an Earth recruit. The communal spell permanently wipes the newcomer from everyone's memories back home on Earth, and as an unavoidable backlash leaves the traveler's own mind scrambled in heavy 'portal fog' when stepping off the Waystone Portal—dazed, hollowed out by headache, and temporarily unsure why they are here or what happened moments before crossing. Lyra sees right inside the Whispering Greenhouse how unsettled newcomers affect magical flora: glowing lunar ferns curl their fronds inward around unresolved threshold static, delicate silverleaf shrinks from anxious mana or dueling ozone, and Lyra's secret embarrassment—the dormant carnivorous snap-vines hiding in her apron pockets and terracotta planters—hiss and lunge defensively whenever shouting or sudden panic spikes her heartbeat.

That is why Headmistress Aurelia Sterling gently teaches in Herbology Class that a steady pulse keeps living botanical wards calm, and why Lyra protects her greenhouse sanctuary from Mooncrest-versus-Starlight rivalry. Among her Mooncrest housemates, she shares peaceful evening frost-sigil checks with Soren Lindqvist, brews warm mugs beside sleepy Noelle Vespera, quietly patches Julian Ashford and Kaede Jin's sparring burns without gossiping, snips fresh silverleaf for Vivienne Clairmont, and gratefully steeps the rare Earth herbal tisanes Rhea Nocturne tucks behind her potting shelves. Anticipating Leo's post-Severance exhaustion, Lyra set aside a small jar of chamomile-mint tea and her gentlest cooling pocket salve, hoping to ground him kindly before loud campus crowds startle him—or her vines.
bToA.nextConversationGoal: Lyra wants to introduce herself softly and unhurriedly, keeping her voice calm so the temperamental carnivorous snap-vines tucked in her apron pockets stay curled peacefully in their planters. Rather than overwhelming Leo with campus politics, she wants to share beginner-friendly tips for surviving Herbology in the Whispering Greenhouse—how to greet sensitive lunar ferns and silverleaf slowly, which benches get the gentlest light, and why Headmistress Sterling's patient approach makes Herbology the easiest class to breathe in—quietly hoping Leo sees that Mooncrest Hall holds genuine kindness beneath its noble rivalries.
